clue.text: Artist in major unconventional ring

indicators.note: something unconventional does not follow the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
a ring is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: An artist is sitting inside a strange ring in some major arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in major' reads like part of the phrase but supplies half the letters; the ring shape adds the final O of the Catalan painter's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Miró was a twentieth-century Spanish surrealist painter and sculptor, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Fly among adjoining nations

indicators.note: something found among others sits inside them, so the letters lie within the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fly buzzing around between two neighbouring countries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like a verb about travelling between countries; it is the noun for the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged insect, one kind of fly in the everyday sense of the word.

clue.text: Setter, maybe, taken with cricket side in turn on way?

indicators.note: one thing taken with another comes along beside it, so the two parts are joined

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog; 'maybe' marks it as an example
the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the side behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: It seems to ask about the crossword's setter joining a cricket team on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the crossword compiler, but here it is the dog breed. In cricket the field divides into the leg side and the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogleg is a sharp bend or angle in a road or golf hole, so it is a turn along a route.

clue.text: Lend poster on politician from Ohio

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing on another sits above it, so the first part comes before the second

blocks.note: a poster is an advertisement, shortened to AD
JD Vance, a politician who was a senator for Ohio

explanation.surface: Someone lends a campaign poster to an Ohio politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Ohio' narrows the politician to JD Vance, the US vice-president who first represented Ohio in the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance money is to pay it before it is due, supplying funds as a loan, so it is a synonym of lend.

clue.text: Source of inflation six ignored in site for mausoleum

blocks.note: a cheeky description of the erectile dysfunction drug
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An economist's remark about inflation near a famous tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of inflation' sounds economic but points to the little blue pill; removing its opening Roman six leaves the Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra in northern India is home to the Taj Mahal, the marble tomb Shah Jahan built for his wife.

clue.text: Deal out second testimonial in support of inspector

indicators.note: in a down clue what supports another sits beneath it, so these pieces follow the other

blocks.note: DI stands for Detective Inspector in the British police
S is the abbreviation for second
a testimonial is a tribute paid to someone

explanation.surface: A card game where a second reference is offered to back up a police inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, pieces that support the inspector are written below the inspector's two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute is to hand out shares among several people, the same sense as dealing cards or portions out.

clue.text: Stop or get off network right away

indicators.note: something sent away is gone, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: to detrain is to get off a train, part of the rail network
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Advice to stop or log off a computer network immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'network' suggests computers and 'right away' suggests at once, but the network is the railway and 'right away' is an instruction to remove R.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain someone is to hold them back or keep them from going, so it matches stop used as a verb.

clue.text: Miserable young guy pocketing nothing for transfer of documents

indicators.note: to pocket something is to put it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: feeling down means feeling miserable
a lad is a young man
zero, nothing, looks like O

explanation.surface: A glum young man pockets no money for handing over paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The young man holds the zero inside him, and the gloomy word goes in front of the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A download is the copying of files from a server or network onto a device, a transfer of data or documents.

clue.text: Pick up chaps for appearance

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: chaps are men, or guys

explanation.surface: Picking up men because of their good looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' looks like a dating phrase but asks the solver to listen for a word that sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A guise is the outward form or look someone adopts, often a disguise, so it means their external appearance.

clue.text: Hit hard (after reversal) in tie

indicators.note: a reversal turns something back to front, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: tonk is informal British slang for striking a ball or person hard

explanation.surface: A sports report: a hard hit after a turnaround in a tied game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tie' tempts the solver to think of a drawn match; it is the knotted kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a fastening made by looping and tightening string or rope, and to tie is to make one.

clue.text: Trick, say, with art deal that’s corrupt

indicators.note: something corrupt has been spoiled and altered from its proper form, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A con artist's crooked sale of a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like it introduces an example, but its three letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone astray is to mislead or deceive them into error, the same sense as tricking them.

clue.text: Sharp techies are experts at this in Google’s rival

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: Bing is Microsoft's search engine, a competitor of Google
information technology is the techies' field

explanation.surface: Clever computer people show their skill at a rival search engine.
explanation.walkthrough: The long middle phrase is a roundabout way of naming the techies' subject, which then sits inside the search engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting remark or wind is cutting and keen, so the adjective is a synonym of sharp.

clue.text: Where one might find a GP, effectively?

definitions.text: Where one might find a GP

blocks.clueFragment: Where one might find a GP
blocks.note: first meaning: a family doctor works in a medical practice
second meaning: actually, as things really work out

explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, Britain's family doctor, who works at a practice or surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both located at a doctor's surgery and, idiomatically, in reality rather than in theory.

clue.text: Explanatory words in top case shortly for analysis

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of the word goes
analysis breaks something into parts and reorders them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter cut

explanation.surface: Notes explaining the key case, briefly written up for study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top case' suggests a leading legal case, but the words are just letters for rearranging after the last E is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Captions are short pieces of text printed beside pictures to describe or explain them.

clue.text: Designate in hearing thing to be screened

indicators.note: in hearing means as it is heard, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: to designate is to choose, or pick

explanation.surface: A court hearing where something is to be screened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' suggests a court session; it signals sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Pic is informal for a picture, a film, which is shown on a cinema screen.

clue.text: Contend with favourite in climax?

indicators.note: something in another sits inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: to come is to reach climax
a teacher's pet is the favourite

explanation.surface: Racing talk: taking on the favourite in the final stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contend with' reads as a phrasal verb, but 'with' just links. The favourite goes inside the verb for reaching a climax.
explanation.definitionFit: To compete is to strive against rivals for a prize or position, the same sense as contend.

clue.text: Teacup regularly taken for Greek character

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A Greek person taking tea as a regular habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, equivalent to T, so it is a written character.

clue.text: Son with mettle ignoring a cause of trouble?

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
mettle is courage or spirit
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirited son who ignores things is a cause of trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first A of the bravery word is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is something that brings great suffering or affliction, like a plague, so it is a source of trouble.

clue.text: Horrific rogue’s disturbed writer

indicators.note: something disturbed is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the possessive read as letters
the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A horror novelist writing about a disturbed villain.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe is ignored so the possessive gives its letters plus S. 'Writer' is a crossword convention for the setter, giving ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome describes something causing horror and disgust, such as grisly violence, a close synonym of horrific.

clue.text: Group curtailed prominent feature in informal discussion

blocks.note: a team is a group; its last letter is cut
a prominent chin is a notable facial feature

explanation.surface: A group cuts short a key topic in a casual chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prominent feature' sounds like a highlight of a talk, but it is a jutting part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A teach-in is an informal lecture and debate session on a topical issue, often held on a university campus.

clue.text: This person’s friend touring old city is lacking sophistication

indicators.note: to tour a place is to travel all around it, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: this person is me, the setter, so this person's is I'm, I am
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: The setter's pal travels round an ancient city and turns out to be naive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person's' stands for I'm, a contraction rather than a possessive. Ur is the crossword's favourite old city.
explanation.definitionFit: Immature means not fully developed or childish, so an immature person lacks worldly refinement.

clue.text: Cuckoo over area patrolled by host is one exhibiting wild behaviour

indicators.note: in a down clue one thing over another sits above it, so it comes first
a patrol goes all the way round its beat, so one piece is surrounded by another

blocks.note: an MC, master of ceremonies, hosts an event
the ani is a black tropical American bird of the cuckoo family
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A crazy person hanging around a place watched over by a host is behaving wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' looks like slang for crazy, which fits the answer's sense, but it names the bird. The ani is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A maniac is a person who behaves in a wildly violent or reckless way.

clue.text: Amount of money (not half) to break rule possibly makes one melancholy

indicators.note: not half means only half is used, so the word loses half its letters
possibly means in some other possible form, so the letters are rearranged
to break into something is to get inside it, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: taken as written
a fund is a sum of money; only its first half is kept

explanation.surface: Breaking the rules for half the cash leaves someone feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of the money word breaks into the rearranged rule, between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rueful means expressing sorrowful regret, so it describes a sad, downcast mood.

clue.text: Moderate Republican beginning to excoriate period of austerity

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

the opening letter
Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moderate Republican' reads as a political type, but 'Moderate' is the definition, a verb. The austerity is religious fasting, not economics.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or ease a stern position, so it means to moderate as a verb.

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for nationalist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A nationalist cheers after a Conservative is kicked out of some political body.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Cs is removed before rearranging. 'a body' suggests a political assembly, but it is the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatomical means relating to anatomy, the structure of a human or animal organism, so it concerns a body.

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch premier' reads as one person; the premier is India's, and 'Dutch' supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Narendra Modi has been India's prime minister since 2014, and premier is another title for a prime minister.

the first and last letters

clue.text: Potentially destructive type kept in asylum, otherwise

explanation.definitionFit: Clothes moth larvae eat wool and fabric, so a moth is a creature that can ruin garments.

clue.text: Absurd situation with fellow leaving daughter describing a rainbow?

indicators.note: what is leaving goes away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a farce is a ridiculous situation

explanation.definitionFit: To describe a curve is to trace its path, and a rainbow forms a bow, so the sky was arced.

clue.text: I mention having to move very quickly
